HAND-WRITTEN FIXTURES, PENDING CAPTURE FROM A REAL ARCH SYSTEM

These files were written by hand from pacman's documented behaviour. They were
NOT captured from a real system, so they show what cronen assumes the output
looks like, not what it looks like. Replace them with captures (see "Needs
checking on Arch" in PLAN.md and the M7 pull request for the commands), keeping
the package set, or update the tests that count on it.

M7, the transaction preview:

  pacman_Sup.txt           pacman -Sup --dbpath <db> --logfile /dev/null --noconfirm
                           --print-format '%n %v %r %s'
  pacman_Si.txt            pacman -Si --dbpath <db> --logfile /dev/null -- <names>
  pacman_Qi-updates.txt    pacman -Qi -- <names>, the installed side of the same packages
  pacman_Qu.txt            pacman -Qu --dbpath <db> --logfile /dev/null (with an [ignored] line)

pacman_Qq.txt gained "iptables" (the package the fixture replacement removes).
The checkupdates database directory (/tmp/checkup-db-1000/sync/) is only
simulated by internal/fixtures.FS().

M9, preflight (see preflight.go):

  fstab.txt                  /etc/fstab, with a /boot entry
  proc_self_mounts.txt       /proc/self/mounts, deliberately WITHOUT /boot
  mirrorlist.txt             /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist, with a file:// mirror first
  lastupdate_mirror.txt      <mirror>/lastupdate (Unix time, 6800 s before the reference)
  lastupdate_reference.txt   https://geo.mirror.pkgbuild.com/lastupdate

The osrelease value, the /usr/lib/modules/<release>/ directory, the /boot kernel
image names and sizes, and the statfs numbers (Disk()) are made up in code. The
embedded files must keep the layout of the real ones (see the M9 pull request for
the commands to capture them).

M8, rebuild detection:

  pacman_Ql-foreign.txt    pacman -Ql -- <foreign names>
  pacman_Si.txt, pacman_Qi-updates.txt: the zstd and mesa blocks gained a Provides
                           line. zstd goes libzstd.so=1-64 -> libzstd.so=2-64 (made up,
                           real zstd keeps its soname) to give one soname change; mesa
                           provides libgbm.so=1-64 in both (an unchanged soname).
  pacman_Qi_gnome-shell-extension-legacy.txt, pacman_Qi_spotify.txt, pacman_Qi_paru-debug.txt:
                           Depends On gained libzstd.so=1-64 / libgbm.so=1-64 entries
                           (soname spelling "libfoo.so=N-64", the spelling the plan says to
                           verify). The packages don't really depend on them.

The ELF files the fake scans (fixtures.Opener) aren't checked in: fixtures.ELF builds
them, a few hundred bytes each, with known DT_NEEDED entries. Capture a few real ones
when verifying on Arch.
M10, security and known issues (hand-written; the AVG ids, CVE ids, project
ids are invented (labels use the real severity::2-high style), and the JSON field names are what cronen assumes
the services use):

  security_all.json          https://security.archlinux.org/all.json (an array of groups)
  gitlab_issues_linux.json   .../api/v4/projects/archlinux%2Fpackaging%2Fpackages%2Flinux/issues
  gitlab_issues_mesa.json    the same for mesa; every other project answers 404
  pacman_Qn.txt              pacman -Qn, the native packages with their versions
  vercmp.txt                 gained the comparisons the security fixtures need
M11, AUR review (hand-written from cgit's documented atom and rawdiff formats):

  aur_atom_<pkgbase>.xml    https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/atom/?h=<pkgbase>
  aur_rawdiff_<pkgbase>.diff  .../rawdiff/?h=<pkgbase>&id=<newest>&id2=<base>
  aur_diff_*.diff           hand-made PKGBUILD diffs, one per suspicious-change heuristic
                            (plus clean ones that must trigger nothing)

M11 update: the shape of the atom feed (urn:sha1:<sha> ids, Z timestamps, http
links with id= before h=), the rawdiff direction (id = new side, id2 = old side),
the .SRCINFO section that rawdiff always includes (ignored by the heuristics)
and the RPC CoMaintainers array were checked against the live AUR (anonymous
GET, 2026-11-05). The commit messages, ids and diff contents are still invented.

aur_info.json: visual-studio-code-bin gained a "CoMaintainers" array, as the RPC returns it.

M13, package browser (hand-written; generated from a compact table, same
package set as pacman_Qq.txt plus their dependencies and a few orphans):

  pacman_Qi.txt       pacman -Qi with no arguments, every installed package. Required By
                      and Optional For are derived from Depends On / Optional Deps. Plain
                      -Qi prints no "Backup Files" field, so the fixture has none (see
                      pacman_Qii.txt). Install Date uses the same spelling as Build Date; the
                      spotify/paru fixtures use the "Mon 01 Sep 2025 10:01:00 AM UTC"
                      spelling, and the parser reads both.
  pacman_Qdtq.txt     pacman -Qdtq (orphans, one name per line)

M14, removal, orphans and housekeeping (hand-written; PENDING CAPTURE from a
real Arch system, see the M14 pull request for the read-only commands):

  pacman_Rp.txt               pacman -Rsp --print-format '%n %v' -- spotify
                              (spotify plus alsa-lib, which -s pulls in)
  pacman_Qii.txt              pacman -Qii -- sudo glibc, cut to Name, Version and
                              Backup Files. HAND-WRITTEN, pending capture: the
                              "path [status]" lines and the column-18 continuation
                              follow what a real pacman 7.1.0 prints; the packages
                              and paths are invented
  pacman_Rp_breaks.stderr     the stderr of pacman -Rp -- libx11: the exact
                              wording of the ":: removing X breaks dependency
                              'Y' required by Z" lines is what cronen assumes;
                              internal/ops also accepts the "Z: removing X
                              breaks dependency 'Y'" spelling
  diff_u_mirrorlist.txt       diff -u /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist <that>.pacnew
  systemctl_failed.txt        systemctl --failed --plain --no-legend
  systemctl_failed_user.txt   the same with --user (nothing failed)

The package cache listing (/var/cache/pacman/pkg/, a few files with sizes set
by internal/fixtures.FS) and /etc/pacman.conf are made up in code.

M15, history and downgrade (hand-written; PENDING CAPTURE from a real Arch
system, see the M15 pull request for the read-only commands):

  pacman.log                  gained transactions: nvidia-utils upgrades, a kernel
                              upgrade that was cut off (no "transaction completed"),
                              a -S that installed one package and removed another,
                              and a -U downgrade of firefox. The ISO timestamps match
                              what pacman 7 writes; the lines are invented
  pacman_Up_unsatisfied.stderr  the stderr of pacman -Up for a package that breaks a
                              dependency. The wording of the ":: installing X (v)
                              breaks dependency 'Y' required by Z" line is what cronen
                              assumes
  (in code) history.go        the answers to pacman -Qip -- <files> (Build Date in the C
                              locale) and pacman -Up --print-format '%n %v' -- <files>
  (in code) fixtures.go       the cache files: linux 6.17.3 (+ .sig) and 6.17.2 (no .sig),
                              nvidia-utils 575.64-1 (+ .sig), firefox 143.0-1 (no .sig).
                              File names assume the epoch-less spelling is not needed:
                              none of these packages has an epoch
  vercmp.txt                  gained the comparisons of those versions

M16, bandwidth helper (hand-written, pending capture; see the M16 pull request for
the read-only commands to capture them):

  proc_net_route.txt            /proc/net/route, one default route over wlan0
  nmcli_metered_*.txt           nmcli -t -g GENERAL.METERED device show wlan0
                                (no, yes, "yes (guessed)", unknown)
  pacman_Ql-repo.txt            pacman -Ql -- firefox vim ripgrep (repo packages' files)

The access times of the files in pacman_Ql-repo.txt (fixtures.FS()) and the
timing samples of --demo (fixtures.DemoUpgradeSamples/DemoPrefetchSamples) are made up
in code.
